Definition: Whether the system enables individuals to authenticate themselves or their documents digitally through electronic verification
Comments: The CNIE contains an electronic chip that stores each citizen's digital identity and enables digital authentication. The NIP (14-character alphanumeric) serves as a unique digital identifier. PKI infrastructure was established as part of the IBOGA/Gemalto/Thales solution to enable trusted digital authentication.

Definition: Whether authentication is possible through a centralized government portal or digital gateway
Comments: Gabon has some digitized government services (e-Tax, e-Visa, driving license registration, business registration). The CNIE is intended to enable access to digitized administrative services. However, the government-wide interoperability platform is not yet operational as of Dec 2024, and CNIE integration into a unified government portal is still being implemented under the World Bank project.

Definition: Whether individuals can view their data held in the ID database and see how it has been accessed
Comments: Act 025/2023 (Personal Data Protection Law) explicitly grants individuals the right to obtain all their personal data in an understandable form, to rectify it, and to request deletion. The APDPVP must respond to access requests from data subjects (Article 52/53). This right extends to data held in the national ID system.

Definition: Whether the system enables Know Your Customer (KYC) packet collection for service provision, particularly financial services
Comments: The CNIE is explicitly accepted for banking services and financial transactions. The World Bank Digital Gabon project document notes that KYC requirements for opening bank accounts require verifiable ID credentials, and the CNIE/NIP is designed to fulfil this role. The UNCDF partnership in 2025 specifically links digital identity to financial inclusion.

Definition: Whether the ID authority and system are subject to general oversight of the courts and judicial review
Value Name: Yes, but not specific to ID
Comments: The 2023 data protection law (Act 025/2023) gives the APDPVP authority to submit observations to the Public Prosecutor, initiate investigations, and impose sanctions. Courts have oversight over APDPVP decisions (data controllers can appeal to the State Counsel). However, the World Bank project notes that the CNPDCP/APDPVP has limited capacity to fully carry out its mandate.

Definition: Whether the civil registration and digital ID systems are integrated
Comments: Civil registration (CR) in Gabon remains largely paper-based. As of December 2024, 0 administrative departments have at least one civil registration office digitally registering vital acts (target: 15 by June 2026). The World Bank Digital Gabon project is funding digitalization of civil registration. Birth registration coverage is high (~90%) but records are not digitally linked to the ID system yet.

Definition: Whether procedural rules for collection, storage, and sharing of ID-related personal data are publicly available and established
Comments: Act 025/2023 establishes rules for data interconnection requiring non-discrimination, appropriate security measures, and proportionality. Cross-border transfers are restricted to countries with adequate protection. The World Bank Digital Gabon project requires that databases of the RBPP, civil registration, and national ID card systems NOT be integrated (kept separate) per legal covenant. Formal interoperability framework with data sharing rules is still under development.

Comments: Law No. 027/2020 of 24 December 2020 specifically governs the Numéro d'Identification Personnel (NIP) and mandates the Ministry of Interior to assign a NIP to every person living on national territory. This is a dedicated digital identity regulation.

Definition: Whether national data protection legislation exists and covers personal data linked to the ID system
Comments: Gabon has a comprehensive Data Protection Act: Law No. 025/2023 of 09/07/2023 amending Law No. 001/2011 of 25 September 2011 on the protection of personal data. This establishes the APDPVP (Authority for the Protection of Personal Data and Privacy) as the supervisory authority.

Definition: Whether a Data Protection Authority or similar body regulates ID data collection and sharing by the ID system
Comments: The APDPVP (Autorité pour la Protection des Données Personnelles et de la Vie Privée) was established under Act 025/2023 as an independent supervisory authority. It is empowered to investigate, subpoena evidence, receive complaints, impose sanctions, and conduct inspections on personal data processing including biometric data used in identity systems.

Definition: Whether the digital ID credential serves as legal proof of an individual's identity as codified in law
Comments: The CNIE is legally recognized as proof of identity for all official transactions including banking, administrative procedures, and is planned as a CEMAC travel document. The NIP attestation is the foundational legal document required for all administrative processes.

Definition: Whether formal legislation (act, law, regulation) governs digital identity including identification acts, digital ID laws, or equivalent legislation
Comments: Gabon has a comprehensive legal framework: Law 027/2020 on the NIP (Personal Identification Number), Law 001/2011 / 025/2023 on personal data protection, Law 26/2018 on electronic communications, and Law 025/2021 on electronic transactions. The Ministry of Interior is mandated to assign NIPs to all persons on the territory.

Definition: Whether the system and the production of credentials can be managed, maintained and developed by in-country technical staff (as opposed to foreign vendors)
Comments: The CNIE system is managed by the Ministry of Interior (DGDI) with technical support from IN Groupe (French company). The World Bank Digital Gabon project provides institutional and financial support. Maintenance responsibilities are shared between government (Ministry of Interior, ANINF) and private vendor (IN Groupe/Thales).

Definition: Whether the Ministry of Finance has oversight of the financing and development of the digital ID system
Comments: The Ministry of Finance is involved in the Digital Gabon project coordination — a joint working session in January 2026 included Ministers of Economy, Finance, and Digital Economy, and launched the Integrated Public Finance Management System (SIGFIP). The World Bank loan is co-supervised with Finance Ministry involvement, but primary ID oversight sits with the Ministry of Interior.

Definition: Whether the ongoing management, maintenance and development of the ID system can be funded by sustainable domestic resources
Comments: The World Bank approved a $68.5 million IBRD loan for the Digital Gabon Project (P175987) effective July 2024 (closing June 2026). Gabon's 2026 digital budget was increased by 156% to 82 billion CFA francs. Long-term sustainability relies on government commitment and external financing; vendor dependency (IN Groupe/Thales) poses some risk.

Definition: Whether the system collects biometric data and which modalities are collected (fingerprints, facial image, iris scans)
Comments: The IBOGA (Identification Biométrique Officielle au Gabon) system captures fingerprints and photographs. The CNIE chip stores biometric data. An Automated Biometric Identification System (ABIS) with fingerprint matching guarantees uniqueness. Full biometric enrollment required for NIP.

Definition: Whether identity records are stored in electronic/digital format versus paper-based records
Comments: The IBOGA (RBPP) system provides a centralized national biometric civil registry serving as the master database for NIP and CNIE. The database is electronic and supports ABIS deduplication. However, civil registration records remain paper-based; digital CRVS integration is still in progress.

Definition: Whether the country has established or is actively developing a national digital identity system, including foundational ID systems that enable authentication across multiple services. Fully deployed means operational nationwide and accepting new registrations.
Comments: Gabon launched the Carte Nationale d'Identité Electronique (CNIE) in June 2024, underpinned by the Numéro d'Identification Personnel (NIP) system (Law 027/2020). The IBOGA biometric registry has been operational since 2012/2013. System is active but nationwide rollout is still in progress.

Definition: Whether the digital ID system is designed to be interoperable across government agencies and with other systems through APIs or data exchange protocols
Comments: A government-wide interoperability framework is planned under the World Bank Digital Gabon Project (P175987) but not yet implemented as of December 2024 (target: June 2026). Some limited e-government services exist (e-Tax, e-Visa) but formal interoperability platform has not been deployed. Score reflects partial/in-progress status.

Definition: Whether credential is accepted or mandatory for opening bank accounts and accessing financial services
Comments: The CNIE is explicitly valid for banking services and financial transactions. The World Bank Digital Gabon project and the UNCDF partnership emphasize CNIE/NIP as the key credential for KYC and financial inclusion. However, 54% of adults remain unbanked (World Bank Findex 2025), and the system is newly launched with limited actual uptake data.

Definition: Whether the digital ID is recognized or interoperable across borders through regional agreements or travel documents
Value Name: Recognized in some regional contexts (e.g., ECOWAS travel)
Comments: Gabon plans to make the CNIE a travel document within the CEMAC (Economic and Monetary Community of Central Africa, 6 countries). Since 2008, CEMAC permits visa-free travel for biometric passport holders. The CNIE is intended to be recognized for CEMAC travel. However, the policy is announced but not yet fully implemented, and the CEMAC biometric passport policy itself faces implementation challenges.

Definition: Whether registration for digital ID is mandatory, optional, or mandatory for specific groups
Comments: Law No. 027/2020 of 24 December 2020 makes NIP enrollment mandatory for all persons on Gabonese territory: 'toute personne physique présente sur le territoire national a obligation à se faire enrôler.' Enrollment in the NIP is compulsory by law.

Definition: Whether credential is accepted or mandatory for accessing public healthcare services
Comments: Gabon's CNAMGS (Caisse Nationale d'Assurance Maladie et de Garantie Sociale) provides universal health coverage and assigns identification numbers to insured individuals. Integration with the NIP/CNIE is targeted under the World Bank Digital Gabon project. Current CNAMGS enrollment uses its own ID system, with NIP linkage in progress.

Definition: Whether non-nationals including refugees, asylum seekers, and permanent residents are eligible to register
Comments: Law 027/2020 mandates a NIP for ALL persons living on national territory, not only citizens. The law explicitly covers non-nationals/residents. A separate foreigner ID card ('carte de séjour') is used for residents, and foreigners must use their ID to access services like SIM registration and bank accounts.

Definition: Percentage of eligible population that has been issued or registered with digital ID credentials
Comments: As of December 2024, the World Bank ISR shows 0% of population 16+ with a NIP (target 90% by June 2026). The CNIE was initially issued only in Libreville (capital) with plans to expand to all police stations nationwide. Government pledges nationwide coverage but rollout is in early stages.

Definition: Whether ID system undergoes regular security audits, penetration testing, or vulnerability assessments
Comments: ITU Global Cybersecurity Index 2024 placed Gabon in Tier 4 (second-to-last) with a score of 39.86/100, noting maximum score in legal measures (20/20) but weak technical, organizational, and cooperation measures. A dedicated Security Operations Center (C-SOC) for government systems is planned but not yet operational as of December 2024 (per World Bank ISR). Law 027/2023 on cybersecurity was enacted.

Definition: Whether credential is accepted or mandatory for SIM card activation and mobile service registration
Comments: Gabon mandates SIM card registration requiring a national ID or passport. ICTworks (2022) confirms Gabon in the list of countries requiring national ID for SIM registration. Foreign residents must use foreigner ID cards for SIM registration. This practice predates the CNIE but the system is being formalized with the new digital ID.

Definition: Whether credential is accepted or mandatory for registering for social assistance programs and accessing social services
Comments: The World Bank Digital Gabon project specifically targets associating 250,000 CNAMGS (National Health Insurance) social protection beneficiary records with a unique legal ID credential (NIP).
